Iteration 1/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: Initial comparison set focuses on measured binary predictors that are plausible biomarkers for pathway-specific or synthetic-lethal dependencies in this lung cell-line cohort. Oncogenic MAPK/RTK predictors are tested against the corresponding dependency scores: KRAS mutation with dependency_KRAS, BRAF V600E with dependency_BRAF, EGFR amplification with dependency_EGFR, and ERBB2 amplification with dependency_ERBB2. MSI-high status is tested against WRN dependency because MSI-high cancers are a recognized context for WRN dependency. KEAP1 loss is tested against NFE2L2 dependency because KEAP1 loss activates NRF2 pathway biology and may increase NFE2L2 pathway dependency. TP53 loss is tested against MDM2 dependency in the opposite direction: TP53-null lines are expected to show less negative MDM2 scores than TP53-intact lines if MDM2 dependency is mediated through p53. SWI/SNF context is tested with SMARCA4 loss against SMARCA2 dependency. MYC amplification is tested against several transcription-, helicase-, proteostasis-, and ribosome-related dependencies, including USP7, DHX9, RPL11, and POLR2A, because MYC-driven states may increase dependence on gene-expression and proteostasis machinery. RB1 loss is tested against KIF18A as a mitotic dependency marker. PIK3CA mutation and APC mutation are tested as pathway biomarkers for STAT3 and TMED10, with uncertain anticipated directions. NF1 loss is tested against RIT1 because NF1 loss alters RAS-pathway signaling, but the direction is less certain.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: Prior to seeing results, I prioritize 12 discovery tests that have the strongest mechanistic rationale for context-specific dependency differences: (1) KRAS mutation on dependency_KRAS and BRAF V600E on dependency_BRAF for MAPK pathway dependencies; (2) EGFR and ERBB2 amplification on their corresponding RTK dependency scores; (3) MSI-high on WRN dependency, an established candidate synthetic-lethal context; (4) KEAP1 loss on NFE2L2 dependency for NRF2 pathway biology; (5) TP53 loss on MDM2 dependency, expected to be less negative if MDM2 dependency is p53-dependent; (6) SMARCA4 loss on SMARCA2 dependency, a classic paralog synthetic-lethality hypothesis; (7) RB1 loss on KIF18A dependency; and (8) MYC amplification against USP7, DHX9, and POLR2A dependencies, representing MYC-associated transcriptional, helicase/replication-stress, and transcription-machinery dependencies. These tests cover 12 of the 16 requested dependency outcomes while deferring three less direct pathway-biomarker hypotheses (H11 PIK3CA-STAT3, H12 APC-TMED10, H16 NF1-RIT1) and one additional MYC-associated hypothesis (H14 MYC-RPL11) for a subsequent batch. The deferred tests are not considered lower priority scientifically, but POLR2A was prioritized over RPL11 in this batch because it tests a more direct transcription-machine dependency that is mechanistically close to MYC amplification. These analyses are exploratory and will be judged by signed effect magnitude, Welch interval uncertainty, and cell sizes; acceptance will be based on whether the observed differences are scientifically meaningful rather than solely on statistical significance.

record.narrative: The signed convention is critical: for direction -1, a positive signed estimate corresponds to a raw exposed-minus-comparator dependency score that is more negative, i.e., stronger dependency. H5 and H8 are clear discoveries: MSI-high lines are more negative on WRN by about 0.79, and SMARCA4-loss lines are more negative on SMARCA2 by about 0.78, with very tight intervals far above any clinically meaningful scale. I accept these in this dataset and keep them active for robustness checks. H6 was registered as KEAP1 loss increasing NFE2L2 dependency, but the signed interval is strongly negative, meaning the raw effect is about +0.80 (less negative dependency), the opposite direction. I reject H6 and propose a direction-reversed claim supported by the same evidence. The remaining results are small and/or uncertain. H3 is borderline: EGFR-amplified lines may have a slightly more negative EGFR dependency, with point estimate around a 10%-of-baseline scale difference, but the interval includes no effect and even a tiny opposite effect. Because this is a clinically relevant borderline signal, I keep it active and request independent validation. H1, H4, H7, H9, and H10 remain unresolved but deferred; their point estimates are small, and although some intervals permit a modest clinically meaningful difference, the evidence is not sufficient to claim a meaningful association. H2 shows no clinically meaningful negative effect and even a small opposite point estimate. H13 and H15 are too small to support clinically meaningful MYC-related differences. Overall, multiplicity and possible technical confounding remain concerns; I propose interaction checks by CRISPR library and subtype for the accepted large effects, while reserving validation here for the borderline EGFR claim where it is most decision-relevant.

  "narrative": "The accepted large dataset effects for WRN/MSI-high, SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss, and weaker NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss are so large relative to the 10% scale that the main issue is not detecting a difference but understanding whether these associations are robust to screen technical and lineage context. I therefore register direct robustness tests in cells with above-median Cas9 activity and above-median screen ROC, and batch-a interaction tests for the same three associations. If the effects persist in high-Cas9/high-ROC cells and are not strongly batch-a specific, they are less likely to be simple technical artifacts, although this still does not establish causality or generalizability. I also keep subtype and library checks active while deferring some less mechanistically direct broad comparisons. For EGFR and ERBB2 amplification, the overall and validated overall results were weak or non-replicated, so I test whether a clinically meaningful context-specific dependency appears within the larger adenocarcinoma subgroup. Finally, I add signaling-extension tests in which EGFR or ERBB2 amplification is associated with STAT3 dependency, a BRAF V600E test of RIT1 in the opposite direction, and an ARID1A-loss test of POLR2A as an exploratory chromatin-remodeling/transcription link. These new hypotheses are falsifiable and will be judged by signed mean differences, uncertainty, and whether they exceed a clinically meaningful scale.",
  "research_notes": "Accepted dataset associations: H5 MSI-high -> much stronger WRN dependency; H8 SMARCA4 loss -> much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; H17 KEAP1 loss -> weaker NFE2L2 dependency. New priority analyses: Cas9-high and screen-ROC-high mean differences for WRN/SMARCA2/NFE2L2; batch-a interactions for the same effects; adenocarcinoma-restricted EGFR and ERBB2 amplification tests; EGFR/ERBB2 amplification effects on STAT3; BRAF V600E effect on RIT1; ARID1A loss effect on POLR2A. record.narrative: The accepted large dataset effects for WRN/MSI-high, SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss, and weaker NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss are so large relative to the 10% scale that the main issue is not detecting a difference but understanding whether these associations are robust to screen technical and lineage context. I therefore register direct robustness tests in cells with above-median Cas9 activity and above-median screen ROC, and batch-a interaction tests for the same three associations. If the effects persist in high-Cas9/high-ROC cells and are not strongly batch-a specific, they are less likely to be simple technical artifacts, although this still does not establish causality or generalizability. I also keep subtype and library checks active while deferring some less mechanistically direct broad comparisons. For EGFR and ERBB2 amplification, the overall and validated overall results were weak or non-replicated, so I test whether a clinically meaningful context-specific dependency appears within the larger adenocarcinoma subgroup. Finally, I add signaling-extension tests in which EGFR or ERBB2 amplification is associated with STAT3 dependency, a BRAF V600E test of RIT1 in the opposite direction, and an ARID1A-loss test of POLR2A as an exploratory chromatin-remodeling/transcription link. These new hypotheses are falsifiable and will be judged by signed mean differences, uncertainty, and whether they exceed a clinically meaningful scale.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

H22 directly tests WRN-MSI within the dominant Avana library. H23 tests ARID1A loss against SMARCA2 dependency, a mechanistically adjacent SWI/SNF question. H35 tests EGFR amplification specifically in adenocarcinoma, the largest subtype-relevant context after the weak overall and nonreplicated EGFR signal. I defer batch interactions, additional library interactions for SMARCA2/NFE2L2, ERBB2/STAT3 amplification tests, BRAF-RIT1, ARID1A-POLR2A, and the remaining broad initial comparisons because current information is higher for accepted-effect robustness and the two high-value follow-ups. Results will be interpreted as signed dataset-specific conditional associations, not causal effects.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

record.narrative: All newly delivered conditional comparisons are interpreted using the signed convention. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed-minus-comparator score is more negative, i.e. stronger CRISPR dependency in the exposed group. For the direction +1 NFE2L2 claims, a positive signed estimate means the raw score is less negative, i.e. weaker dependency in KEAP1-loss cells. The new evidence substantially strengthens the three large prior associations within this dataset. SMARCA4-loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency not only overall but also in adenocarcinoma, above-median Cas9 activity, and above-median screen ROC cells (H20/H27/H30). MSI-high is associated with stronger WRN dependency overall and in adenocarcinoma, Avana-library cells, above-median Cas9 activity, and above-median screen ROC cells (H21/H22/H26/H29). KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency overall and in the same strict contexts (H25/H28/H31). These conditional signed effects are approximately 0.78 to 0.80 with very tight intervals and cell counts satisfying the 20-per-cell rule. That magnitude is far beyond a 10% relative-scale criterion using the absolute mean dependency scores, and the intervals exclude trivial or modest effects. The consistency across adenocarcinoma, library, and high-quality technical subsets makes these findings less likely to be artifacts of a single screen context, although they still remain dataset-specific associations and not causal claims. I therefore accept the due conditional associations and close the redundant robustness checks. I also close the earlier accepted H8/H17 investigations because the new evidence sufficiently documents context stability for those associations; H5 remains active because I am requesting independent validation for it. H23 shows no support for the hypothesized clinically meaningful stronger SMARCA2 dependency with ARID1A loss: the signed estimate is small and negative, and for the proposed stronger-dependency direction the upper bound corresponds to only about 5.5% of the SMARCA2 mean scale, below the 10% threshold. I reject that directional claim and close it; this does not prove there is no effect, only that the registered hypothesized clinically meaningful association is unsupported. H35 remains unresolved because EGFR-amplified adenocarcinoma cells have a positive signed point estimate of about 0.020, below the 10% scale, but the interval still permits a clinically meaningful stronger EGFR dependency up to roughly 20%. Given the exploratory subgroup nature and the weak/nonreplicated overall EGFR signal, I do not accept it. I propose an interaction test (parent H35) to determine whether the adenocarcinoma EGFR-amplification contrast differs from its complement, which is a cleaner heterogeneity test than treating H35 as an isolated subgroup. The main concern for the large effects is not statistical detection but residual technical confounding, multiplicity from many targeted tests, and generalizability. The large accepted effects are so far above the threshold that multiplicity is not a serious threat, but the smaller EGFR and ARID1A follow-ups are more vulnerable to overinterpretation. I request one independent validation for H5 because MSI-high association with WRN dependency is the largest and most potentially important finding; independent replication will improve confidence in the dataset-level association without implying causality or generalizability.

record.narrative: New validation result. H5, MSI-high versus dependency_WRN, has now received independent validation. The independent signed mean difference is +0.821 with a strict independent interval from 0.766 to 0.877; both comparison cells are valid and the effect is in the hypothesized direction, meaning MSI-high cells have much stronger WRN dependency than MSI-non-high cells in this dataset. This agrees with the discovery result +0.790, 0.760 to 0.819, and is far beyond a 10% relative-scale criterion for dependency-score differences. I therefore accept H5 and close it as an established dataset-specific association. This remains a measured association within this lung line panel, not causal proof or an established external generalization. Overall supported dataset findings: MSI-high lines show much stronger WRN dependency; SMARCA4-loss lines show much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; and KEAP1-loss lines show weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The latter two remain strong and robust across several conditional subsets, including adenocarcinoma, Avana-library, above-median Cas9 activity, and above-median screen ROC contexts, but they have not yet received the same independent validation as H5. Negative or unsupported directional findings include H2, H6 in its original direction, H13, H15, and H23: these do not support clinically meaningful stronger dependency as proposed. H3, EGFR amplification versus EGFR dependency, is not supported enough to accept: discovery and validation point estimates are near or below the 10% threshold and intervals cross zero, although the upper bounds allow small effects; I leave it unresolved as non-prioritized possible small uncertainty. Many other small signals remain unresolved because their estimates are below or near the clinical threshold and uncertainty intervals remain compatible with null. The most informative next analysis is to test whether the accepted large associations persist under less favorable technical conditions and alternative library context. I registered direct lower-Cas9 refinements for WRN/MSI-high, SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss, and NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss, plus direct non-Avana tests for SMARCA2 and NFE2L2 where cell counts are more plausible. The already registered library, batch, adenocarcinoma-complement, EGFR/ERBB2, RIT1, STAT3, and POLR2A comparisons remain appropriate for understanding context dependence and possible smaller effects. No new validation is requested now because the highest-priority independent replication, H5, is complete; future validation should be reserved for a newly discovered large and robust effect.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The strongest evidence so far concerns three large dataset-specific associations: MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, and KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. These are already robust across adenocarcinoma and high-quality screen subsets, and WRN/MSI-high has independent validation. Because only 12 analyses can be advanced at a time, I defer currently active but unevaluated redundancy checks (batch, library, low-Cas9, and several small EGFR/ERBB2/RAS follow-ups) to allocate slots to higher-information new comparisons. The new proposals test three useful extensions. First, if MSI-high induces replication/transcription stress, it may not only affect WRN but also DHX9, POLR2A, or USP7; these are falsifiable hypotheses expecting more negative dependency in MSI-high cells. Second, if MYC expression reflects proliferation or transcriptional state, it may modify or at least confirm the accepted large associations within a MYC-high context; I register direct mean differences in MYC-high cells for the three accepted exposure-outcome pairs. Third, I test biologically linked p53/MDM2/USP7/MYC and SWI/SNF-to-transcription hypotheses: MYC amplification may strengthen MDM2 dependency, TP53 loss may weaken USP7 dependency, and SMARCA4 loss may strengthen POLR2A dependency. Finally, I add RAS-pathway cross-dependency tests: BRAF mutation may associate with KRAS dependency, KRAS mutation may associate with BRAF dependency, and KRAS mutation may weaken RIT1 dependency. Signed estimates are interpreted directly: negative signed values support stronger dependency for direction -1 claims, and positive signed values support weaker dependency for direction +1 claims. Given dependency-score means around 0.09–0.42, the 10% clinical threshold corresponds roughly to 0.01–0.04 score units, so many cross-pathway effects may remain clinically non-meaningful unless they are unusually large. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations, not causal claims or external generalizations.
